title: Onprem CI signer workflow + TF hooks playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook documenting an opinionated CI/CD signer workflow and Terraform hook pattern for private (VPC / on-prem / airgapped) deployments. Goal: provide a repeatable, auditable, and minimally-invasive pipeline that produces signed, attestable artifact bundles and asserts a minimal set of preflight + post-deploy checks before enabling traffic. This doc covers:

- CI stages and responsibilities (build, sign, attest, promote)
- Terraform module interface hooks for release gating and artifact provenance
- ArgoCD / GitOps integration notes for digest pinning, rollbacks, and canary signals
- Edge cases for airgapped and VPC-only customers (artifact bundles, local registries)
- Operational runbook entries and quick commands for incident recovery

Assumptions / constraints:

- Customers run a private GitOps repo that mirrors a canonical upstream release repo.
- We require cosign-based image signing and LinkedAttestation for Helm charts.
- Artifact promotion should use immutable digests whenever possible (no mutable tags in prod).
- Terraform applies are gated by signed attestations generated in CI; TF must be able to validate attestations before applying.
- Minimal trust boundary: the signer (CI) is considered semi-trusted; we allow key rotation and vault-backed key material (HSM/KMS) integrations.

Core CI workflow (opinionated pipeline):

Stages (ordered):
1) build (CI builder job)
   - Build container images with standard labels: git_sha, build_ts, pipeline_id, base_image, vuln_scan_summary_url
   - Produce Helm chart tarball + chart metadata (Chart.yaml, values.schema.json)
   - Output: image artifacts (registry or local cache), chart artifact (tgz), SBOMs (syft cyclonedx), and wasm/sidecar artifacts if any

2) scan & policy (policy runner)
   - Run vulnerability scan (Trivy or Snyk); produce a summarized JSON report 
   - Run policy checks (e.g., no root user, resource limits present, disallow debugging flags)
   - If policy fails, pipeline marks as FAILED and attaches reports

3) sign & attest (signer job, uses Cosign + in-toto style attestations)
   - Sign each image digest with cosign; publish OCI artifact signature to registry OR bundle signatures into an artifact-bundle (.tar.gz) for airgap customers
   - Produce attestations describing: source git ref, CI pipeline id, SBOM pointer, vulnerability score, chart checksum, terraform-module-id
   - Store signature and attestation metadata in a signed provenance.json stored in the release bucket or artifact repository
   - Key management: prioritize KMS/HSM-backed keys. For ephemeral test keys, ensure a TTL and a notes file in provenance.

4) promote (release manager job)
   - Create release entry in release repo: release/<semver>-<digest>.yaml containing digests, signatures, attestations links
   - Attach smoke test scripts (small curl/healthcheck) and a minimum rollout strategy (canary pct, interval)

5) terraform apply (operator-initiated or automated with gating)
   - Before TF runs: validate that the release entry contains signed attestations and that the signatures match the image digests that will be referenced in Terraform variables
   - Run a preflight terraform plan that includes a validation step (small helper) that fetches attestations and verifies signature freshness and SBOM presence

Terraform module notes (interface and hooks):

Design goals: modules should be small and declarative, expose an explicit "release" input that is digest-based, and provide a hook to fail-fast if attestations are missing or invalid.

Suggested module interface (example, as plain keys):
- variable "release_manifest" { type = string }   # path or URL to release YAML that lists images and digests
- variable "attestation_check" { type = bool default = true }
- variable "attestation_source" { type = string default = "https://release-bucket.redwood.internal" }
- output "validated_release" { value = string }

Hook contract (pseudo):
- During 'terraform plan' the module runs an external data source (local-exec or terraform external) that:
   1) fetches the release_manifest
   2) for each image digest, fetches cosign signature and attestation (or unpacks artifact-bundle)
   3) verifies signatures against the configured key(s) or keyserver
   4) validates the SBOM presence and vuln score threshold
   5) returns a single boolean and message that will be used by the module to fail the plan if not satisfied

Implementation notes (practical):
- Prefer a small helper binary (signed-verify) shipped with infra repo that performs steps 1-4 and returns exit codes/messages. Keep it hermetic.
- Use Terraform external data source to run signed-verify so plan fails early in CI.
- For airgap customers, the release_manifest can be a local path (file://) and signed-verify knows how to unpack local artifact bundles.

ArgoCD / GitOps integration patterns:

Two recommended flows:
A) Digest-driven GitOps (preferred)
   - GitOps repo contains a release manifest that pins container images to digests.
   - ArgoCD watches for changes to this manifest.
   - Promotion = commit to repo (release manifest update).
   - Rollout: use ArgoCD App of Apps + canary controller (flagger or Argo Rollouts) reading the rollout strategy attached to the release manifest.

B) Operator-controlled TF apply with GitOps for infra state
   - Infra repo contains TF variables referencing the release digest; PRs to infra repo trigger TF plan and the TF external data source validates attestations as above.
   - Merge gating: require signed attestations and a passing smoke check status as part of PR checks (GitHub status check or GitHub Actions gating).

Argocd considerations:
- Use imageUpdater sparingly; prefer commit-based updates.
- Enable "path-based" sync windows to coordinate multi-app rollouts.
- For airgapped clusters with private registries, ensure ArgoCD has access to the registry credentials (sealed secrets or vault integration).

Image signing and attestation details:

- Cosign as primary signing mechanism. Use keyless verification only as transitional; prefer KMS-backed keys for production.
- Signatures must be attached to digest (not tag). Storing only tag signatures is insufficient.
- Attestations schema (recommendation):
  {
    "release_version": "string",
    "git_ref": "string",
    "pipeline_id": "string",
    "sbom_url": "string",
    "vuln_summary": "LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH",
    "chart_checksum": "sha256:...",
    "signer": "principal@redwood"
  }
- For Helm charts, produce a signed chart provenance file (helm package --sign) and include cosign signatures for chart OCI artifacts.

Airgap and VPC edgecases:

- Artifact bundles: tar.gz containing images (as oci-layout), signatures, attestations, and SBOMs. Customer provides a local registry push script.
- Terraform path: when using local bundles, module must accept a local bundle path and perform verification against the embedded attestations rather than remote keyserver.
- Key rotation: provide a migration path for rotating keys: re-sign with new key, publish rotation metadata in release_manifest with old_keys and new_keys list. Terraform validation should accept either key during a 7-day grace window.

Canary and rollback strategy (playbook steps):

1) Promote release -> commit release_manifest with canary strategy (5% for 10 minutes, then 25% for 20 minutes)
2) Argo/rollouts applies canary; smoke checks run against canary endpoints (auth tokens provided by ops)
3) If smoke checks fail -> automated rollback (Argo Rollouts) + open hotfix ticket and mark release as FAILED in release registry
4) If smoke checks pass, continue to gradual rollout and finally mark release as SUCCESS

Runbook quick commands (operator):

- Verify a release attestation locally:
  signed-verify --manifest https://release-bucket/release-1.4.2.yaml --keyserver https://kms.redwood.internal --require-sbom

- Manually unbundle an airgap artifact and push to local registry:
  tar -xzf release-1.4.2-bundle.tar.gz && ./push-to-registry.sh --bundle ./oci-layout --registry my.registry.local:5000

- Force rollback in ArgoCD:
  argocd app rollback <app> <previous-revision> --server argocd.internal:443

- Re-sign a digest with rotated key (emergency helper):
  cosign sign --key kms://projects/.../keys/new-key sha256:<digest>

Open questions / discussion items (to resolve before GA):

- Should Terraform performs signature verification during plan or only at apply? (pros/cons: plan fails fast vs. risk of plan/app drift)
- How to best surface attestation failure reasons to non-engineering operators? (UI in console vs. structured logs)
- Do we require a canonical release registry for Hosted customers vs allow arbitrary registries for private?
- What SLA do we provide for key rotation and re-signing assistance for enterprise customers?

Milestones / next steps (short term):

- Build signed-verify helper and include in infra repo (owner: Diego) – 2026-03-01
- Prototype TF external data source that runs signed-verify in plan (owner: Priya) – 2026-03-10
- Create a small PoC with Argo Rollouts + release_manifest commit flow for canary signals (owner: Evan) – 2026-03-18
- Document airgap bundle format and provide push-to-registry helper script (owner: Aisha) – 2026-03-22

Appendix: rough artifact-bundle layout (plain text)

release-1.4.2-bundle.tar.gz/
  oci-layout/                <-- OCI images export (skopeo/oras style)
  images/                    <-- image tarballs referenced by digest
  charts/                    <-- helm tgz files
  attestations/              <-- signed JSON attestations (cosign attachments)
  sboms/                     <-- cyclonedx files and syft summaries
  provenance.json            <-- top-level signed manifest listing everything
